lessonTitle: §1.4 · Cơ sở, span và tọa độ

auditSummary.reason: All differences are lexical or display-level. Canonical rendering can be applied downstream without altering approved mathematical content.

canonicalNotation.meaning: Target vector space; must be declared before basis claims.
The i-th vector in an ordered generating family or basis.
Ordered family; order is semantic data.
Coefficient column aligned to ordered family B.
Coordinates of vector v in ordered basis B.
Column matrix whose order matches B.
Reconstruction residual in a compatible representation.
Map from source-basis coordinates B to target-basis coordinates E.
Kronecker delta used in orthonormality conditions.
Euclidean norm when the metric is the standard inner product.

canonicalFormulaRegistry.name: Linear combination
canonicalFormulaRegistry.meaning: Build v from ordered directional contributions.
canonicalFormulaRegistry.condition: All vectors belong to the same compatible vector space.

canonicalFormulaRegistry.name: Span
sourceAliases: span(b_1,...,b_k) = {sum_i c_i b_i | c_i in R}
canonicalFormulaRegistry.condition: The family belongs to one vector space.

canonicalFormulaRegistry.name: Span membership
sourceAliases: v in span(B) iff exists c such that B_mat c = v
v in span(B) iff exists c: B_mat c=v
canonicalFormulaRegistry.condition: Ambient coordinates and metadata are compatible.

canonicalFormulaRegistry.name: Linear independence
sourceAliases: sum_i z_i b_i = 0 implies z_i = 0 for all i

canonicalFormulaRegistry.name: Basis condition
canonicalFormulaRegistry.canonicalText: B basis of V ⇔ span(B)=V and B independent
canonicalFormulaRegistry.displayLatex: B\text{ is a basis of }V\iff\operatorname{span}(B)=V\text{ and }B\text{ is linearly independent}
sourceAliases: B is a basis of V iff span(B)=V and B is linearly independent
B basis of V iff span(B)=V and B independent
canonicalFormulaRegistry.meaning: Spanning gives existence; independence gives uniqueness.

canonicalFormulaRegistry.name: Coordinates
canonicalFormulaRegistry.condition: B is an ordered basis of the target space.

canonicalFormulaRegistry.name: Reconstruction
canonicalFormulaRegistry.condition: Matrix columns, basis order and version match.

canonicalFormulaRegistry.name: Uniqueness
canonicalFormulaRegistry.canonicalText: B_mat c=B_mat d and B independent ⇒ c=d
sourceAliases: B_mat c = B_mat d and B independent imply c=d
B_mat c=B_mat d and B independent imply c=d
canonicalFormulaRegistry.condition: c and d refer to the same ordered family.

canonicalFormulaRegistry.name: Orthonormal shortcut
sourceAliases: c_i = v · b_i when b_i · b_j = delta_ij
canonicalFormulaRegistry.condition: The basis is verified orthonormal in the same inner-product space.
canonicalFormulaRegistry.methodNote: For orthogonal non-unit vectors use c_i=(v·b_i)/(b_i·b_i); this is a method condition, not a new formula ID.

canonicalFormulaRegistry.name: Coordinate change
canonicalFormulaRegistry.meaning: Convert source-basis coordinates B to target-basis coordinates E.
canonicalFormulaRegistry.condition: Both are ordered bases of the same space and direction is explicit.

canonicalFormulaRegistry.name: Residual
canonicalFormulaRegistry.condition: Vector and reconstruction share schema, units, frame and metric.

canonicalFormulaRegistry.name: Dependent-family non-uniqueness
canonicalFormulaRegistry.canonicalText: B_mat z=0, z≠0, B_mat c=v ⇒ B_mat(c+t z)=v
sourceAliases: if B_mat z=0, z!=0 and B_mat c=v, then B_mat(c+t z)=v
canonicalFormulaRegistry.meaning: A nonzero null relation creates infinitely many coefficient vectors.

unitAndQuantityRules.rule: Attach the unit to the complete scalar or coordinate result, not to basis directions when they are dimensionless.
Keep route heading and robot yaw labels distinct.
Keep timestamp alignment and transform-age statements in prose or metadata, not inside coordinate formulas.
State when a reported value is norm squared rather than norm.
Basis directions may be dimensionless only when the physical model explicitly defines them that way.

semanticStyleRules: Use lowercase bold symbols for vectors in display math when renderer support is available.
Use B for an ordered family and B_mat or bold B for its column matrix; do not silently merge the two meanings in prose.
Use the zero vector symbol in vector equations and component zero only when referring to one scalar component.
Use ∈, ∃, ⇔ and ⇒ in display math; use Vietnamese prose around the formula for explanation.
Use P_{target←source}; never infer direction from nearby prose alone.
Keep coordinate brackets [v]_B intact as one semantic token.
Keep transpose attached to the whole coordinate tuple.
Use dot product · rather than an asterisk.
Keep residual and norm claims separate from physical-validity claims.
Do not introduce a fixed numerical tolerance without a documented scale and source.

globalRules: One primary mathematical claim per formula block.
Meaning and conditions must stay adjacent to the formula they qualify.
A warning must not be visually detached from the formula or example it constrains.
Do not split a coordinate token, matrix row or transform subscript across semantic blocks.
Examples must separate setup, calculation, result and interpretation.
Long worked cases may use numbered steps; ordinary sections should not imitate slide numbering.
Do not repeat the same full formula in consecutive blocks unless the second occurrence performs a new derivation or check.

resolvedDisplayVariants.issue: F3 uses both 'such that' and colon notation.
resolvedDisplayVariants.resolution: Display uses ∃c: B_mat c=v; prose explains existence.

resolvedDisplayVariants.issue: F4 alternates between z_i=0 for all i and z=0.
resolvedDisplayVariants.resolution: Display uses vector statement z=0; prose may expand to all components.

resolvedDisplayVariants.issue: B and B_mat may appear close together.
resolvedDisplayVariants.resolution: B names ordered family; B_mat or bold B names its column matrix.
Display uses centered dot with stable operand grouping.

resolvedDisplayVariants.issue: Orthogonal non-unit quotient appears as a warning rather than formula ID.
resolvedDisplayVariants.resolution: Keep it as F9 method note; do not create F13.

resolvedDisplayVariants.issue: Residual norm and norm squared can be conflated.
resolvedDisplayVariants.resolution: Always label residual norm separately from squared vector norm.

resolvedDisplayVariants.issue: Velocity units appear in prose and tuples.
resolvedDisplayVariants.resolution: Attach m/s to complete scalar or coordinate result consistently.

resolvedDisplayVariants.issue: Section density varies by artifact role.
resolvedDisplayVariants.resolution: Apply layer-specific density profiles rather than one universal word or block quota.

downstreamMapping.rendererBoundary: Pass 14 may bind canonical display forms to existing Reader Pro behavior, but may not alter mathematical meaning.

mustPass: All four approved source layers and versions are recorded.
No semantic or worked-case conflict exists.
F1-F12 each have one canonical text and one display form.
Ordered family, column matrix, coordinate column and transform direction remain distinct.
Vector zero and scalar component zero are not conflated.
Orthogonal non-unit handling remains a condition of F9 and does not create new mathematics.
Velocity, angle, time and squared-norm units are unambiguous.
Layout rules are semantic and contain no pixel, CSS, JavaScript or animation instructions.
No approved source artifact is rewritten solely for lexical spacing differences.
E235 remains unchanged and is referenced only as a compatibility baseline.
No Reader Pro or runtime file is changed.
